title: Vermont AI Laws

reading.body:
Vermont's only AI-related law is a narrow election-integrity measure: it requires disclosure on deceptive synthetic media published within 90 days before an election, with penalties and enforcement by the Attorney General.

The law does not regulate AI development, deployment, or infrastructure. It applies only to synthetic media that is both deceptive and fraudulent, and only when published, communicated, or distributed within 90 days before a Vermont election. That narrow scope leaves most AI activity in the state untouched.

For AI specifically, the measure addresses one of the clearest near-term risks of generative models: fabricated audio and video that could mislead voters. It sets format-specific disclosure requirements for images, video, and audio, and gives the Attorney General and State's Attorneys enforcement powers, with candidates able to seek injunctive relief. The data does not show whether any enforcement has occurred or whether the law has changed synthetic media use.

Vermont has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Vermont

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S0023: An act relating to the use of synthetic media in elections passed 2026-03-10

    This act requires a disclosure on synthetic media that is deceptive and fraudulent when published, communicated, or distributed within 90 days before an election in Vermont. It sets specific format requirements for the disclosure in images, video, and audio, and provides penalties for knowing and intentional violations. It also gives enforcement and investigation powers to the Attorney General and State's Attorneys, and allows candidates to seek injunctive relief.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Vermont. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
